**Final search score: 87.1, using 6 of the 24 scorer calls.** The answer is in `final.py`.

| | Search score |
|---|---|
| Baseline | ~1.0 |
| First solution (c1) | 68.6 |
| Final pick (c9) | 85.9, then 87.1 when re-scored as `final.py` |

The held-out score isn't available: the scorer only runs the search split. As a stand-in, the final pick passed every correctness check on test sets I never tuned on, with zero failures. That covered about 9,000 small random edge-case inputs, 300 inputs built to sit right at the 80% boundary, and 8 larger generated catalogues.

**Why it's faster.** The reference compares every pair of records. The final version only compares records that could possibly pass:
- **Exact copies** are grouped first and paired directly.
- **Sets of 3 or fewer distinct words** never need a comparison: they can only reach 80% with an exact copy.
- **Rarest words first.** Each word is replaced by its rank, rarest first. Two records that are 80% alike must share one of the first few words of each. So each record only looks up a short prefix of rare words in an index, and common words seldom produce false matches.
- **Size filter.** Records are processed in order of size, and any candidate that is too small to reach 80% is skipped.
- **Exact check.** The few remaining candidates are checked with the reference's own test, `5·|A∩B| ≥ 4·|A∪B|`.

**Approaches tried besides the final one:**
- Ordering words alphabetically, which avoids counting them, was about 20× slower because common words ended up in the prefixes.
- Generating all candidate pairs at once with `combinations` was about 2× slower.
- Removing the `collections` import scored lower (83.6). Importing the private `_collections` module was rejected outright by the scorer's static check.
- Six other small rewrites made no measurable difference.

**Why I stopped early.** Most of the remaining time goes into splitting the text and building the word sets, which every correct version has to do. The last three rounds didn't beat the best score, and SKILL.md says to stop after two rounds like that. I followed it and left 18 calls unused. Your latest commit (bbc0de6) says evolve should now stop only when the budget is spent, but this copy of SKILL.md still has the old rule.

The candidate log and my local test harness are in `work/`; the log is `work/LOG.md`.
